ops.name: Bookkeeper
ops.description: Staff member who prepares and sends monthly invoices to clients.

ops.name: Firm Owner
ops.description: Owner who oversees billing, sets rates, and reviews payments.

ops.name: Client
ops.description: Business the firm bills monthly for bookkeeping services.

ops.name: Client
ops.description: A business the firm provides bookkeeping services to.
ops.example: Acme Landscaping, billing@acme.com, $450/mo, billed on the 1st

ops.name: Invoice
ops.description: A monthly bill sent to a client for services rendered.
ops.example: Invoice #1042 for Acme Landscaping, $450, sent Mar 1, due Mar 15

ops.name: Line Item
ops.description: A single charge listed on an invoice.
ops.example: Monthly bookkeeping, 1 x $450 = $450

ops.name: Payment
ops.description: Money received from a client against an invoice.
ops.example: $450 received Mar 12 by bank transfer for Invoice #1042

ops.name: Service
ops.description: A billable service the firm offers with a standard rate.
ops.example: Monthly bookkeeping, $450, monthly

ops.name: Statement
ops.description: A summary of a client's invoices and balance over a period.
ops.example: Acme Landscaping, Q1, $1,350 billed, $0 due
Bookkeeper creates Invoice #1042 for Acme Landscaping on Mar 1
Bookkeeper adds 'Monthly bookkeeping $450' to Invoice #1042
Bookkeeper emails Invoice #1042 to billing@acme.com
Bookkeeper records $450 payment for Invoice #1042 on Mar 12
Bookkeeper marks Invoice #1042 paid after full payment
Bookkeeper adds Acme Landscaping with a $450 monthly rate
Firm Owner sets 'Monthly bookkeeping' rate to $450
Firm Owner reviews Acme's Q1 statement showing $0 balance
Firm Owner voids Invoice #1039 created in error
Bookkeeper generates a Q1 statement for Acme Landscaping
Client receives Invoice #1042 by email

ops.text: Every invoice must have a unique, sequential invoice number.
ops.example: After #1042 the next invoice is #1043, never a repeat.

ops.text: An invoice cannot be sent until it has at least one line item with an amount.
ops.example: Invoice #1042 stays a draft until 'Monthly bookkeeping $450' is added.

ops.text: Recorded payments for an invoice may never exceed the invoice total.
ops.example: A $450 invoice cannot accept a $500 payment.

ops.text: A paid invoice cannot be edited; it must be voided and reissued instead.
ops.example: To fix a paid #1042, void it and create #1043.

ops.text: Only the Firm Owner may void an invoice.
ops.example: A Bookkeeper cannot void #1039; only the Owner can.

ops.text: Only the Firm Owner may change a client's monthly rate.
ops.example: A Bookkeeper cannot change Acme's $450 rate.

ops.text: An invoice is marked paid only when payments equal the full amount.
ops.example: #1042 stays unpaid until the full $450 is received.

ops.text: Each invoice must be tied to exactly one client.
ops.example: Invoice #1042 belongs only to Acme Landscaping.

ops.text: No online payment processing or card collection; clients pay by their own method.
No client login or self-service portal in the first version.
No payroll, expense tracking, or general accounting features.
No automatic tax calculation or filing.
No automated recurring billing; invoices are created by staff each month.

ops.question: Who needs an account to use the app?

options.label: Nobody logs in — one person uses it on their own device
Exactly one person logs in (the owner)
Several people log in, possibly with different powers

ops.question: Do different people have different powers?

options.label: Everyone who logs in can do everything
An owner/admin plus staff with fewer powers
Admins define their own roles and permissions

ops.question: Do outside parties (customers, clients, vendors) use the app directly?

options.label: They open a secure link (no account needed)
They have their own accounts and log in

ops.question: Is this for one business, or will many separate businesses use it with their data kept apart?

options.label: Many separate businesses, each seeing only its own data

ops.question: How do additional people get access?
How do people sign in?
What happens when two people edit the same thing at once?

options.label: Common; the app must prevent or merge conflicting edits

ops.question: Do you need a record of who changed what and when?

options.label: Just created/updated by whom and when
A full, viewable history of every change

ops.question: How does the app reach people when something happens?

options.label: It doesn't — people check the app

ops.question: Must it work without internet?

options.label: Keeps working offline and syncs later

ops.question: Where is it used?

options.label: In a browser, on desktop and phone
In a browser, mostly on phones

ops.question: Do you start with existing data?
Do people need to get their data out?
When something is deleted, what really happens?

options.label: It's archived and can be restored
Records are never deleted, only voided/cancelled

ops.question: How much data will there be?
Does it need to connect to other tools?

options.label: A few key ones (e.g., accounting, payments, calendar)
Many — it needs a public API / webhooks

ops.question: Does money move through the app?

options.label: It records payments that happen elsewhere
It collects card/bank payments via a provider
It collects payments and pays out to others (marketplace-style)

ops.question: Languages and regions?
Can files/photos be attached to things?

options.label: Yes — with previews, versions, and sharing

ops.question: Do some actions need someone else's approval first?
Must anything happen automatically on a schedule?

options.label: Records get created automatically (recurring invoices, appointments, reports)

ops.question: Does it hold data with special legal handling (health, payment cards, minors)?
How long is data kept?

options.label: Each business sets its own policy

ops.question: Can each business customize the app?

options.label: No — everyone gets the same thing

ops.question: What do people need to see across many records?

options.label: A dashboard with totals and counts

ops.question: Who sends invoices to whom?

options.label: The business bills its own clients
The business sends invoices on behalf of its clients to their customers

ops.question: How are invoices numbered?

options.label: Strictly sequential per business (no gaps; legally safe)

ops.question: Can an invoice change after it's sent?

options.label: No — corrections go through a credit note / new invoice

ops.question: How do payments get recorded?

options.label: Someone marks invoices paid by hand
Clients pay online and it's recorded automatically

ops.question: Can an invoice be paid in parts?

options.label: No — paid in full or not

ops.question: How is tax handled on invoices?
One currency or several?
Recurring invoices (e.g., monthly retainers)?

options.label: Yes — created and sent automatically on a schedule

ops.question: What happens when an invoice is overdue?

options.label: Someone sends a reminder by hand

ops.question: Late fees?
Estimates/quotes before invoices?

options.label: Yes — and an accepted quote becomes an invoice

ops.question: Corrections and refunds?

options.label: Credit notes plus refunds through the payment provider

ops.question: Track time and bill hours?

options.label: Yes — tracked hours become invoice lines

ops.question: How do invoices reach clients?

options.label: A link to an online invoice page (where they can also pay)
Email with PDF and a link

ops.question: Connect to accounting software?
How detailed is the invoice lifecycle?

options.label: Draft → Sent → Viewed → Partially paid → Paid / Overdue / Void

ops.question: Branding on invoices?
Deposits / retainers up front?

options.label: Yes — deposits that later apply to invoices

ops.question: Do invoices need to carry the customer's purchase order (PO) number?

options.label: No — invoices don't track customer PO numbers
Yes — an optional PO number field is printed on the invoice for the client's records
Yes — required per client, and the system blocks a second invoice against the same PO

ops.question: Can discounts be applied to invoices?

options.label: A single discount on the whole invoice
Per-line discounts and an overall invoice discount

ops.question: What payment terms do invoices carry (when is payment due)?

options.label: Net terms (e.g., Net 15/30/60) counted from the invoice date
Configurable per client or per invoice

ops.question: How do automatic reminders escalate?

options.label: Two gentle nudges: a few days before and after the due date
Weekly reminders after the due date until paid
The firm sets a schedule per client

ops.question: How is an automatic late fee calculated?

options.label: A percentage of the balance, added monthly

ops.question: How are credit notes numbered?

options.label: They share the invoice number sequence
They have their own CN- sequence

ops.question: Can people change many records at once?

options.label: No — one record at a time
Yes — select many and assign/move/tag/delete together

ops.question: What happens when someone tries to remove a Client that has invoices or recorded payments?

options.label: Block deletion while any invoice/payment exists
Archive client but keep all invoices/payments intact

ops.question: How does the app handle the same Payment or Send action fired twice (double-click, retry)?

options.label: Warn and ask to confirm the second time
Record both — user must undo manually

ops.question: How are line-item amounts and currency precision handled?

options.label: Round to cents; reject zero/negative line amounts
Round to cents; allow negative lines (adjustments/credits)
No enforced rounding or sign rules

ops.question: When a client's Billing day (e.g. the 31st) doesn't exist in a month, when is the invoice/due date set?

options.label: Use the last day of that month
Roll forward to the next valid day
Everyone billed on a fixed day regardless

ops.question: An invoice is marked Sent but the email delivery fails — what state results?

options.label: Keep as draft/unsent until email confirmed sent
Mark sent but flag delivery failure for retry
Mark sent regardless of email outcome

ops.question: Can invoice states be reversed (unsend a sent invoice, reopen a paid one)?

options.label: No reversal — only void and reissue (per r4)
Allow unsend/edit until viewed, then void-only

ops.question: When the Firm Owner is unavailable, can a Bookkeeper be delegated void/rate-change rights (r5/r6)?

options.label: Owner can grant temporary delegated rights
Bookkeeper requests; action queued for Owner approval

ops.question: When an invoice is voided, what happens to its sequential number (r1)?

options.label: Number stays voided in place — a visible gap remains
The number is freed and reused by the next invoice
Only issued invoices consume numbers; voided drafts don't

stated in the description: The firm bills its own clients monthly.
stated in the description: r1 requires unique sequential invoice numbers.
stated in the description: No automatic tax calculation (g4).
stated in the description: No automated recurring billing (g5).
stated in the description: Bookkeeper records payments and marks invoices paid by hand (a4, a5).
stated in the description: Domestic firm billing in one currency.
stated in the description: One firm, one country/language.
stated in the description: r4: a paid invoice cannot be edited (must be voided/reissued), implying editable while unpaid.
stated in the description: r4 and a9 use voiding/reissuing rather than deletion of invoices.
stated in the description: Ordinary business billing data; no health/card/regulated data (g1).
stated in the description: Staff create invoices each month; no scheduled automation (g5).
stated in the description: No accounting/payroll integrations in scope (g1, g3).
